headlines.title: Giants broadcaster Mike Krukow says goodbye in emotional speech after final game
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Mike Krukow has known all season that this would likely be the end, and he made it official in early August. He has had a long time to think about what goodbye might look like, and what he might want to do over his final weekend as a broadcaster at Oracle Park. The beginning of it was something he could not have scripted. Krukow visited the clubhouse on Friday afternoon to see some longtime friends, but right as he entered, he encountered relievers Jason Foley and Sam Hentges. It was an odd coincidence. The two offseason additions were available to the Giants because they were coming back from shoulder injuries, the ailment that ultimately ended Krukow’s career as a pitcher and led to a second life within baseball. There was no doubt that this would be the most emotionally exhausting weekend of Krukow’s life, but as it started, he was right in his comfort zone. He was in a clubhouse. He was talking pitching. He was giving the two advice on how to strengthen their shoulders, hoping it would help the Giants. Does it get any better than that? Over the next three days, the Giants would get swept, but for Krukow, the rest of the send-off was perfect. The final weekend ended on the field, with an emotional and entertaining ceremony that was watched by thousands of fans who stayed long after the final out of a disappointing season. Kruk and longtime partner Duane Kuiper were given the keys to the city of San Francisco and told that the 27th plaque on the portwalk beyond right field will honor their final game together. Earlier in the weekend, former MLB umpire Ed Montague stunned Krukow with the scorecards from the first game ever played at Oracle Park. Kuiper was the final speaker before Krukow’s goodbye message, and he read from a long list of random things he will miss about his partner, including his mastery of menus, the rhino yawn, their time calling a popular video game, and their days spent roller blading. “That’s right. I know. Look at us,” Kuiper said, grinning. “But there was a time when we were swishing around Chicago.” Kuiper noted that Krukow has been happy over these past two months, and that was in part because they were able to be together. A couple of weeks ago, Kuiper vowed to Krukow that he would not miss his final game despite ongoing treatment for throat cancer, and he held up his end of the bargain. When it was his turn, Krukow led thousands in shouting the home run calls of the other Giants broadcasters, and he threw in a touching tribute to Greg Papa, who is going through his own health battles. He ran through a long list of references to Giants legends, with the loudest reaction coming when he noted that everyone wanted to “Let Timmy smoke.” Krukow then took some time to say thanks, not just to his broadcast partners and notable Giants like Bruce Bochy and Barry Bonds, but also to dozens who worked behind the scenes on TV, the radio and within the organization. He finished his speech by thanking the fan base and shouting a reference to the championship parades. “It is a privilege for all of us who ever played here to represent the city on the field, in the front office and in the broadcast booth,” he said, surrounded by his family. “As I sit here before you today, we can say one more time, ‘We are the Giants! We are San Francisco! And we will never forget you!’ Thank you!” The day ended with thunderous applause. Hours earlier, the first of more than a dozen standing ovations came after the first inning, when the broadcasters’ grandchildren gathered in front of the booth and revealed that it had been renamed the Kruk and Kuip Broadcast Booth. True to form, the two spent very little time celebrating. Kuiper immediately joked that he was going to use a sharpie next season to rename it the Kuiper Broadcast Booth, and that led into a conversation about an Oracle Park alteration that he did make earlier in the morning. Just before 9 a.m., Kuiper walked through the left field gate as he always does, but he didn’t take his usual path past the home dugout and up to the third floor. He met Giants vice president of media relations Matt Chisholm on the outfield grass, and the two went out to right field to put up a stick figure version of Kuiper next to the “Atta Babe, Kruk!” sticker that’s been out there since he announced his retirement. Kuiper even added a round belly. Krukow admitted later that he was melancholy coming to the ballpark — until he saw the right field wall. “A stick figure with a boiler,” he said on the broadcast. “Oh my lord. That’s too good.” It was a light moment in a broadcast filled with them. There have been plenty of tears over the last six weeks, but the two got to go out with a close game, one that allowed them to analyze but also have quite a bit of fun. In the eighth, they showed that they’re as good as ever. Christian Koss, the last man standing from the Opening Day roster, appeared to hit a go-ahead homer right down the left field line. Kuiper went into his home run call, but the Dodgers challenged, and as the video was pulled up, he quipped, “If that’s called foul, one of us is going to quit.” The replay officials in New York ruled it had hit the net just to the left of the pole, and Krukow exclaimed, “No way!” Kuiper astutely pointed out that third base coach Gary Pettis, who had the best view, had seen it all the way and was the only one on that side of the field who wasn’t upset. The Giants were inches away from giving Krukow a thrilling sendoff. Instead, they ended their season in the only way they possibly could. Reliever Duncan Davitt allowed four runs in the ninth, adding one more bullpen meltdown to the pile. With a 5-1 loss, the Giants finished 65-97, the fourth-worst record in franchise history. Krukow was the best player on the only 100-loss team the Giants have ever had, and over the past four decades he has seen the highest highs and lowest lows. On his way out, he focused on the title years and the dynasty, and made sure to let his partner know that the Kuiper Suite at the Krukow home in Reno will be well stocked with popcorn whenever he wants to visit. “I love you, partner,” Krukow said to Kuiper. “Thank you.” Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: Couple accused of killing son-in-law at Dublin Sports Grounds, police said
headlines.description: The suspects in the killing of a man at Dublin Sports Grounds on Saturday are the victim’s parents-in-law, Dublin Police Services said on Sunday. Authorities said a Dublin Police Services sergeant was driving near the Dublin Sports Grounds around 3:08 p.m. when he saw a man lying on the ground in the parking lot and stopped to investigate. At the same time, dispatch received many calls reporting the shooting, according to officials. Responding officers found 40-year-old Jonathan McKinsey of Dublin in the middle of the parking lot with multiple gunshot wounds, according to police. McKinsey was pronounced dead. Officers found and detained two suspects, who were identified as 77-year-old Shouyong Zhang and 77-year-old Shili Chen, police said. Authorities said the suspects are a married couple and are McKinsey’s parents-in-law. Authorities said this is an ongoing investigation.

headlines.title: Zandalasini scores 22, leads Valkyries past Wings 104-80 in Game 1 of first- round playoff series
headlines.description: Cecilia Zandalasini scored 22 points, Gabby Williams added 20, and the second-seeded Golden State Valkyries ran away from the Dallas Wings by halftime for a 104-80 win in the teams’ playoff opener Sunday night. Paige Bueckers had 21 points on 9-for-10 shooting and six rebounds for Dallas, which won seven of eight to end the season to earn the seventh seed and will now try to stave off elimination at home. Game 2 in the best-of-three series is Wednesday in Dallas and, if necessary, Game 3 would be Friday back at Chase Center in front of the raucous, violet-clad sellout home crowd in “Ballhalla.” “Ballhalla’s part of us,” coach Natalie Nakase said of the fans. Tiffany Hayes had 21 points off the bench as the second-year Valkyries scored their most points ever, and Veronica Burton contributed 10 points. Zandalasini shot 7 for 11 with four 3-pointers. The Valkyries outscored Dallas 37-11 in the second quarter and went 10 for 20 from 3-point range in the first half on the way to a 58-31 advantage at the break. The Valkyries shot 18 for 36 on 3-pointers in the game. This marked Golden State’s first true home playoff game after losing to the Minnesota Lynx by one point last year 50 miles away at the NHL San Jose Sharks’ home, SAP Center. The Laver Cup tennis showcase had booked Chase Center before the Bay Area had even been granted an expansion team. In 2025, the Valkyries made history becoming the first expansion organization to reach the playoffs in their inaugural season. Bueckers made 7 of 8 first-half shots and scored 17 by halftime but she didn’t have much help. Dallas went just 6 for 20 from deep. “When we’re awake we’re ferocious on defense,” Nakase said. Kayla Thornton’s 3-pointer at the 7:23 mark of the second quarter put Golden State ahead 32-24 and she pumped her arm as the Wings called timeout. Thornton had 10 points. The Valkyries won seven of eight to finish the regular season and have now beaten Dallas in all four 2026 meetings. ___ AP WNBA: https://apnews.com/hub/wnba-basketball

headlines.title: Pair of earthquakes strike in Northern California
headlines.description: Two earthquakes, with magnitudes of 3.3 and 2.6, struck Northern California on Sunday morning, according to the United States Geological Survey. The first earthquake, with a magnitude of 3.3, hit at 7:21 a.m. and was centered about 20 miles east of Alum Rock, the USGS said. The second earthquake, with a magnitude of 2.6, hit at 7:40 a.m. and was centered around the same area, according to the USGS. headlines.title: San Mateo County buys 74-unit apartment building to provide affordable housing for teachers, school staff
headlines.description: The San Mateo County Board of Education, the San Mateo County Office of Education, and the Housing Endowment and Regional Trust of San Mateo County have partnered to purchase a 74-unit apartment building intended to provide below-market housing for local educators and school staff, county officials announced earlier this month. HEART purchased the San Mateo property with financing that includes a loan from the County Office of Education and bonds issued by HEART. The development was built in 2021 and is currently occupied. Existing tenants will remain, while units that become available will gradually be offered to eligible county office employees and school district staff at below-market rates, according to county officials. The housing will be available to teachers, paraeducators, counselors and other employees who serve students in programs operated by the county office. HEART expects the building to be fully occupied by San Mateo County educators within 10 years. “We are committed to finding creative solutions to address the affordable housing needs of the community, and are proud to partner with the County Office on this project,” said Armando Sanchez, HEART’s Executive Director.

headlines.title: San Francisco man convicted of DUI after 911 caller reports suspected drunk driver on U.S. 101
headlines.description: A 37-year-old San Francisco man was convicted of driving under the influence after a 911 caller reported seeing a suspected drunk driver on U.S. 101, the San Francisco District Attorney’s Office said on Wednesday. Daniel Schuhmacher was convicted by a jury of driving under the influence stemming from an unspecified incident on May 8, 2025, prosecutors said. San Francisco police received a 911 call at about 9 a.m. reporting a suspected drunk driver on southbound U.S. 101 near Paul Avenue. A California Highway Patrol officer responded and was alerted by the caller, who said Schuhmacher was driving behind them. CHP officers moved Schuhmacher to a safe location near Beatty Avenue and Alana Way and conducted a DUI investigation before arresting him, according to prosecutors.

headlines.title: 43rd Annual Folsom Street Fair takes over San Francisco's SoMa neighborhood Sunday
headlines.description: The 43rd annual Folsom Street Fair is taking place Sunday in San Francisco’s SoMa neighborhood. The event runs from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. along Folsom Street, spanning between Eighth and 13th streets in the SoMa district. Admission to the fair is free, though donations are accepted at the entry. Attendees and commuters are advised that local street closures and San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency Muni reroutes remain in effect through early Monday morning to accommodate the festivities.

headlines.title: Stolen mini labradoodle ‘Easton' recovered in San Francisco, suspects detained
headlines.description: A mini labradoodle named Easton was safely recovered and reunited with its owner just hours after being stolen last week. Around 5:45 p.m. Sept. 23, San Francisco Police Department officers assigned to Northern Station responded to Lombard and Webster streets regarding a stolen mini labradoodle dog, “Easton.” The victim reported that she briefly left her dog tied up to go into a daycare center. When she came outside, her dog was nowhere to be found. Responding officers immediately began searching the area and issued a department-wide notification. While coordinating with the SFPD Real Time Investigation Center and the San Francisco Sheriff’s Office, officers identified the suspects’ location on the 200 block of Golden Gate Avenue. SFPD Drug Market Agency Coordination Center officers responded to assist with the investigation. Approximately two hours after the dog was taken, officers observed the suspects and the dog emerging from a doorway. Officers immediately detained the suspects and recovered the stolen dog. SFPD officers notified the victim and arranged for her to reunite with her dog at Tenderloin Station.

headlines.title: 1 injured after shooting on Bay Bridge
headlines.description: A person was hurt following a shooting on the Bay Bridge Saturday morning, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said the shooting was reported around 4:06 a.m. on eastbound I-80, east of Treasure Island, on the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge. Authorities said the victim reported he had sustained a gunshot wound in the leg and was self-transporting to a local hospital for treatment. CHP said all eastbound lanes of I-80 on the Bay Bridge were closed for approximately an hour due to the investigation. An additional search was conducted just after 2 p.m., which closed eastbound lanes for around 30 minutes, CHP added. Authorities said they are working to identify the suspects in the incident and asked anyone with information to contact the CHP tip line at 707-917-4491.

headlines.title: Volunteers mobilize to search new trails for missing Oakland coffee shop owner
headlines.description: A group of volunteers is mobilizing Sunday to search unexamined hiking trails in Oakland and Berkeley, holding onto hope that a major new clue will finally lead them to the 52-year-old coffee shop owner who has been reported missing for just over six months. Amy Hillyard, co-owner of Farley’s coffee shops, was last seen walking near her Oakland home on March 25, having left behind her phone and wallet. Now, her family and friends have a renewed sense of hope following a digital breakthrough in the case. Private investigator Steve Fischer, hired by the Hillyard family, said a deep digital forensics dive of her home computer revealed she spent 33 minutes looking at eight different hiking trails in Oakland and Berkeley the morning before she disappeared. According to Fischer, five of those trails were previously unexamined and have not yet been searched. “This is the biggest break in the case since I’ve been on board. I told the family there’s no guarantees here, but we are going on something that feels like we’re not searching blindly. We actually have a reason for being in these areas,” Fischer said.

headlines.title: Man dead after shooting at Dublin Sports Grounds
headlines.description: A man died following a shooting at the Dublin Sports Grounds on Saturday, Dublin Police Services said. Dublin Police Services said officers responded to a shooting around 3:08 p.m. at 6700 Dublin Blvd. Authorities said a man was found on the parking lot with multiple gunshot wounds, and he was pronounced dead at the scene. Officials said all known suspects are in custody but did not specify the number of suspects involved.

headlines.title: Valkyries excitement continues ahead of WNBA playoffs
headlines.description: The Golden State Valkyries are making another historic run into the playoffs, and the Bay Area is getting ready for “Ballhalla” on Sunday night. Chase Center, Thrive City and sports bars across the Bay Area will be covered in violet and rocking as they cheer on this second-year expansion team while it continues its unbelievable rise in the ranks of the WNBA. Thom Jensen has the full report in the video above.
